units.function: Large embedded-Postgres suite for registry-defined built-in Agent bundles, including asset fallback, lazy/automatic provisioning, hire approval, Adapter validation, typed readiness, managed instructions/skills/routines, drift/reset, immutable markers, uniqueness/concurrency repair, default permissions and proposal-confirmation workflows.
units.dependencyDirection: Static first-party definitions/assets flow into BuiltInAgentService and startup reconciliation; the service composes generic Agent, Approval, Instruction, Skill, Routine, Permission and Interaction services plus database uniqueness/managed-resource bindings. Operators may configure/reset while reconciliation maintains identity/default resources without overwriting detected content drift.
units.keyDataModels: Built-in definition/key/features/defaults/allowed Adapters/models, Agent marker/status/config/budget/reportsTo/permissions, hire Approval payload, managed resource kind/key/current/stock hash and drift status, Skill version, Routine/trigger/schedule, config revision, proposal Interaction/target revision, partial unique index and reconciliation counters.
units.lifecycle: Registry validation rejects duplicate/invalid/default-disallowed definitions. Ensure lazily creates one marked Agent, validates Adapter/model and derives not_provisioned/needs_setup/ready/paused states. Policy-gated creation freezes a pending Agent and approval payload; approval restores the snapshot and materializes resources. Startup can auto-provision paused zero-budget bundles, grant suggestion capabilities, repair display metadata and missing bindings, preserve operator-modified content, reconcile duplicates and continue other Companies. Explicit reset restores selected stock resources. Routines remain disabled until a board enables them; accepted coaching proposals are applied only in a later step.
units.testAssessment: Thirty-plus rich tests cover real schema constraints, concurrent provisioning, legacy duplicate repair, pending approval tamper resistance, Adapter/model allowlists, typed errors, resource drift/hash/reset, startup fault containment, default-disabled automation, least-privilege suggestion grants and accept/reject proposal flow. Major gaps: signed package provenance/version/dependencies/migrations/rollback/uninstall, transactionality across Agent/Skill/Routine/grants, crash injection and outbox, explicit responsible human/data grants, package upgrade compatibility, malicious assets, resource ownership conflicts, approval digest for setup/reset/apply, multi-node reconciliation locks and proof that later execution uses the displayed proposal bytes.
units.designRationale: Deliver opinionated product capabilities as idempotent managed bundles while preserving operator customization, existing governance gates and safe disabled defaults; recover automatically from legacy duplicates or partial materialization without making startup brittle.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a trustworthy FDE/industry-template mechanism that packages organization structure, Agent/Connector roles, instructions, workflows, data policies and Agent Boss views, supports local customization and can upgrade or exit cleanly.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT uniqueness, idempotent materialization, managed-resource bindings, stock/current hash drift, selective reset, disabled automation, strict Adapter capabilities and approval-aware plans as the primary reference for TemplatePackage. Replace hardcoded vendor models/Agents with capability requirements and Connector bindings; add signed manifest/license/SBOM, semantic versions, dependency/migration/rollback/uninstall, atomic plan/apply receipts, organization/data/responsibility objects and explicit owner consent for grants or reset.
units.responsibilityConflict: First setup can apply previously unknown Adapter config and budget without a new approval merely because an empty Agent row already exists. Startup reconciliation auto-adds permissions and undeletable Agents. Missing asset files silently fall back to embedded text. Most critically, the follow-up apply helper checks only that an Interaction was accepted, then writes caller-supplied nextInstructions without verifying it matches the displayed diff/target revision; approval A can authorize execution B. Duplicate repair also keeps the oldest row and cancels the newer approval without evaluating which revision humans approved.
